explanation: Fires on the word that states the posture, configuration or visible state of a just-named body part or light source, peaking right after that noun: 'mouth open', 'eyes closed/wide', 'legs spread/crossed', 'palms toward', 'lights (which) flashed', 'sun shone', 'stars twinkled above' (0.4-0.85 of max). A weaker technical offshoot (0.3-0.7) fires on 'on' after relational nouns ('Effect on', 'bounds on'), on 'zero' after 'is', and on 'definition'/'posited'. Predicted inactive (whole-text peak below 0.25 of max, measured near 0): everyday narrative or instructional sentences of 5-15 tokens that name no body part, light source or technical relational noun (e.g. 'The cat sat on the mat.', 'We drove home on the highway.'). The same state word after a non-body, non-light noun ('book closed', 'papers spread', 'news spread', 'shop is open') also stays below 0.25. Outside this class: arithmetic expressions with ' +'/' -' after 'Let ... be' (up to ~0.7) and some Greek/Korean subword pieces, which this hypothesis does not cover.
